title: Bill Ackman’s $14 billion bet beyond the Magnificent 7
detail:
Bill Ackman’s $14 billion bet beyond the Magnificent 7
Opeyemi Babalola
Tue, November 17, 2026 at 4:33 PM CST 4 min read
^GSPC
META
PS
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For three years, plenty of ordinary portfolios ran on seven engines. Anyone with an S&P 500 index fund leaned on the tech giants known as the Magnificent 7, whether they meant to or not.

That reliance got a rude reminder on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026. The group lost more than $1 trillion in market value in one session, CNBC reported, on fears that the AI data center buildout could slow.

Bill Ackman had already been taking chips off that table. Pershing Square Inc. (PS), the firm he runs, sold about a third of its Microsoft (MSFT) shares in the third quarter, according to its latest 13F filing and the one before it. It also trimmed Meta Platforms (META) by roughly 11%, the filings show.

Also read: Billionaire Bill Ackman's market warning resurfaces as stocks plunge

The more telling number is what stayed.

Leaving aside its own firm and fund, Pershing held about $14 billion in stocks outside the Magnificent 7 on September 30, 2026, based on the latest filing. Those stakes make up nearly 70% of the portfolio.

Ackman trimmed Big Tech while it was rallying

The timing is the interesting part. Microsoft rallied hard in the quarter, so selling a third of the shares only shrank the position from about $2.3 billion to $2.1 billion, per the two filings. Meta's stake even grew in dollar terms.

That looks like housekeeping, not a verdict on Big Tech, and it came weeks before the November rout.

At Sept. 30 prices, the Microsoft shares sold were worth about $1.1 billion, based on the filings. Pershing's new Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) stake was worth about $1 billion, per the 13F.

Ackman effectively swapped a slice of Microsoft for the owner of the New York Stock Exchange.

ICE and Alcon are the newest names in the book

Neither appeared in the June filing, and the semiannual report of Pershing Square USA (PSUS), the firm's listed fund, says both were bought after June 30. Pershing called ICE a simple, predictable cash generator whose shares fell on worries it sees as unwarranted.

The second buy was Alcon (ALC), the Swiss maker of contact lenses and eye surgery gear. Pershing's stake was worth about $954 million at quarter-end, per the 13F.

The report argues that Alcon's roughly 20% operating margin sits well below its potential.

Netflix (NFLX) was the only existing holding Ackman added to. Pershing raised its stake by about 18% to 15.4 million shares, per the filings, even as the stock slipped.

The firm, which briefly owned Netflix in 2022, wrote that the company "has since effectively won the streaming wars."
